You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>

Given the chest radiograph in Figure 1, which of the following findings is most consistent with an acute pulmonary embolism without infarction? Consider the signs that can be directly observed in the X-ray image and how they correlate with specific types of pulmonary embolism.

A) Bilateral pleural effusion and multifocal consolidation in the lower lung fields
B) Oligemia of the left upper lung zone and elevated left hemidiaphragm
C) Hampton's hump in the right lower lung field
D) Bilateral discoid atelectasis and cavitation in the upper lobes
E) Enlarged cardiac silhouette with left-sided pleural effusion
F) Air bronchogram in the right middle lobe
